findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow has no explicit lifecycle state machine. The struct allows any combination of is_validated/is_sent without enforcing valid transitions (e.g., sent without validated, or re-sending after already sent).
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct a BudgetWorkflow in an invalid lifecycle configuration (e.g., is_sent=true with is_validated=false), and mark_sent can be called repeatedly without checking prior state.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with an explicit enum typestate such as enum BudgetStage { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Constructors enforce valid transitions; the enum owns lifecycle data so Option is unnecessary.

findings.problem: status is a pub String. Any caller can set it to any string value (e.g., "foo", "", "SENT", "sent"), making the domain state space unbounded and unenforceable.
findings.failure_mode: callers can assign arbitrary strings to status, breaking invariant that status must be one of a known set (draft/validated/sent). Comparison becomes case-sensitive string equality rather than enum variant match.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a domain enum: enum BudgetStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }. Remove the separate status field and is_sent boolean; encode transitions in the enum variants.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent booleans with no invariant enforcing their relationship. They represent a two-bit state machine (4 combinations) but only 3 are valid.
findings.failure_mode: callers can set is_sent=true while is_validated=false (sent without validation), or set both to true simultaneously without an ordered transition. No enforcement of the single-source-of-truth for lifecycle.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single enum typestate: enum BudgetStage { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. The enum variants enforce valid states and carry lifecycle data in the variant that owns it.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate optional field coexisting with a boolean is_sent, allowing sent_at_epoch_ms to be Some without is_sent=true, or is_sent=true without sent_at_epoch_ms being Some.
findings.failure_mode: callers can leave sent_at_epoch_ms=None while is_sent=true (sent with no timestamp), or set sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(x) while is_sent=false (timestamp without being sent). The Option is a dangling lifecycle field not owned by a variant.
findings.fix: Fold sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant: enum BudgetStage { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. This makes the timestamp present only when the budget is sent, eliminating invalid Option/bool combinations.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain invariants. Any string (empty, unbounded, non-unique) is accepted as a budget ID. Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors.
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct a BudgetWorkflow with an empty string, whitespace, or otherwise invalid id. The domain cannot enforce rules like minimum length, format, or uniqueness. id is not a newtyped primitive.
findings.fix: Create a BudgetId newtype with a smart constructor: pub struct BudgetId(String); impl BudgetId { fn new(s: &str) -> Result<Self, BudgetError::InvalidId> { ... } }. Parse hostile input once at the boundary into trusted BudgetId; the core consumes BudgetId, not String.

findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow exposes all fields as pub with raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>). There is no parse boundary: callers can construct the struct directly with any values, bypassing validation. Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: any code in the crate (or downstream crates) can instantiate BudgetWorkflow with id="", status="bogus", is_validated=false, is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=None — an internally inconsistent and invalid domain object with zero validation at construction.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a single fallible constructor or builder that validates invariants (e.g., validated before sent, sent requires timestamp). Replace raw primitives with domain types (BudgetId newtype, BudgetStage enum). The public API becomes: impl BudgetWorkflow { fn new(id: BudgetId) -> Self { ... } fn validate(&mut self) -> Result<(), BudgetError> { ... } fn mark_sent(&mut self) -> Result<(), BudgetError> { ... } }.

no profiler evidence that BudgetWorkflow layout is cache-optimal
no allocation analysis: mark_sent creates String via "sent".to_string() on every call instead of using a static enum variant
no second-ring evidence for zero-cost abstraction claims

residual_risk: Static review only. The crate has severe typestate violations: status as String instead of enum, independent lifecycle booleans instead of a unified state machine, dangling Option lifecycle field, raw String ID without newtype, and no parse boundary. A caller can construct any invalid state combination at compile time. The mark_sent function adds String allocation per call instead of using enum variants. These are fundamental architectural defects requiring full enum/typestate replacement, not incremental repairs.
